decisions.executionNote: Holder is in the right workspace, pens left. Begin elbow-up right-arm reorientation for a side grasp, keeping left clear.
Advance the right hand toward the holder while completing the horizontal inward-facing side-grasp orientation.
Replan after continuity rejection: retain the current near-horizontal grasp orientation and use smaller translations toward the holder.
Bring the open right jaws around the holder's side at mid-height; keep orientation and elbow configuration continuous.
Holder appears displaced by the forward jaw. Withdraw laterally with jaws open before realigning, rather than continuing to push it.
Realign the right gripper forward of its previous contact, with a small yaw adjustment away from the wrist singularity. Holder retention has not yet been established.
Use a short raised forward adjustment then approach the holder laterally with open jaws. Geometry is uncertain after contact, so keep increments small.
Clear the holder upward with open jaws to stop lateral pushing and obtain a safer realignment view.
Holder has tipped onto its side. Reorient the right gripper above it for a top-down recovery grasp, preserving the elbow-up branch.
The recovery rotation was rejected before motion. Retry with one-fifth angular increments to remain on the continuous IK branch.
Continue the top-down recovery approach above the fallen holder, with clearance before descending.
Align the downward-facing right gripper over the fallen holder's body. Keep jaws open and maintain height until alignment is visible.
After the IK interruption, lower the recovery approach with reduced rotation and translation increments, keeping the current elbow branch.
Wrist view places the holder against one jaw rather than centered. Shift across the aperture with slight clearance, then descend only a little.
Center the fallen holder between the jaws and lower the gripping region around its body, rather than closing on the top surface.
The forward alignment reached the IK boundary. Stop advancing and lower vertically in small increments to improve reach margin and straddle the holder.
Lower slightly around the fallen holder and close the right gripper. Retention will be checked with a small lift, not inferred from the command.
Lift the closed right gripper back toward reachable space and check whether the holder follows before attempting to restore it upright.
The holder follows the wrist during the lift. Begin a gradual upright rotation while moving back from the reach boundary; keep the grip closed.
Continue bringing the retained holder upright and inward, keeping the cup clear of the table and the left workspace.
Finish a cautious upright adjustment of the retained holder while beginning the left-arm approach to the pens. Keep the hands in their own workspaces.
Lower the held cup to an accessible insertion height and remove its remaining sideways tilt. Move the left gripper above the cyan pen while rotating toward a top-down grasp.
Maintain the now-upright holder and complete the left top-down orientation above the cyan pen before descending.
Cyan pen is aligned across the open left jaws. Shift along its length toward a useful grasp point, then lower while keeping the holder steady.
Descend the aligned left gripper around the cyan pen, with a small along-pen correction. Keep the right holder fixed and closed.
Close on the cyan pen and perform a short vertical retention test while holding the upright cup steady.
The cyan pen follows the gripper. Raise and rotate it tip-up while moving toward an above-rim insertion approach; keep the right-hand holder stationary.
Complete the cyan pen's upright rotation and approach above the holder with extra vertical clearance before insertion.
Align the cyan pen's lower end over the cup opening while retaining height; the head view suggests it is still left and nearer than the opening.
The cyan pen's lower end is now at the opening. Make a small centering correction and lower it into the upright held cup.
Seat the cyan pen slightly deeper, release it inside the holder, and withdraw upward to inspect whether it remains inserted.
Cyan remains in the holder after release. Withdraw left and reorient above the purple pen for the next top-down grasp, keeping the cup fixed.
Approach above the purple pen while continuing the top-down reorientation, leaving clearance until the jaws are aligned.
Complete the downward-facing left grasp orientation while approaching the purple pen from above. Keep the filled holder upright and fixed.
After the IK continuity interruption, lower first to regain reach margin and use much smaller rotation increments while aligning over the purple pen.
Move slightly toward the purple pen's cap and lower the open jaws around its upper body, finishing the small downward alignment correction.
Center the purple pen across the aperture and close around its upper body. Start only a tiny lift to check retention without dragging it.
Lift the purple pen away from the table and retreat from the reach boundary, beginning a gentle upright transfer rotation only after clearance.
Purple remains retained. Raise it to insertion clearance while rotating its capped end upward, away from the holder until nearly vertical.
Finish rotating the purple pen upright and bring it above the holder, maintaining clearance over the rim and the inserted cyan pen.
Lower the upright purple pen into the free side of the holder beside the cyan pen, using a small forward centering adjustment.
Contact has tilted the holder, so stop pushing. Release the purple pen at its current insertion depth and withdraw upward to inspect settling and retention.
Purple fell onto the table. Restore the held cup toward upright without releasing cyan, while withdrawing left and preparing to pick the yellow pen.
After the right-arm continuity interruption, first clear the left gripper from the cup and cyan pen. Retry the holder correction only with small rotation increments.
Lift and retract the right hand to regain wrist/reach margin before correcting the holder tilt. Continue the left approach above the yellow pen without descending to contact yet.
Raise the held cup while gently correcting its tilt, so the wrist has room to rotate. Continue aligning the left gripper above the yellow pen.
Bring the holder slightly forward and lower without further wrist rotation. Finish aligning the open left jaws over the yellow pen for a controlled descent.
Lower left jaws around the yellow pen's upper body. Change the right hand's approach azimuth gently to free wrist margin while maintaining its hold on the cup.
Close on the yellow pen and test with a small lift. With improved wrist margin, gently restore the cup toward upright without releasing it.
Lift the retained yellow pen clear before rotating. Reorient the right approach around the holder so it can be lowered without exceeding the wrist's continuous configuration.
Rotate the lifted yellow pen toward upright. Correct the holder's visible forward/right tilt with a small opposite rotation, reducing the saturated right wrist bend.
Finish orienting the yellow pen upright. Lower the restored holder to a reachable insertion height and bring it closer to the center without crossing the arms.
Keep the yellow pen clear while adjusting the holder's forward tilt to expose its opening. Raise the right wrist during the correction to preserve joint margin.
Hold the yellow pen clear and bring the cup back toward the robot, lowering it modestly while easing the right wrist bend. This should give a reachable, visible insertion approach.
The yellow pen's lower end is at the cup rim. Make a small rightward centering correction and shallow insertion, keeping the holder still.
The cup shifted during shallow insertion, so withdraw yellow immediately. Roll the held cup cautiously to identify and expose its opening rather than continuing to push against an obscured surface.
The holder appears to have slipped toward an axial grip. Keep yellow clear and tilt the right approach downward while raising it, to expose the cup mouth and recover an upright orientation.
Continue the slow downward recovery rotation of the retained holder, with yellow held clear. Inspect its mouth and axis before another insertion attempt.
The cup mouth appears directed sideways. Lift clear and correct both sideways and forward tilt while keeping yellow stationary; verify the holder axis again before approaching it.
Cyan has fallen out, so no insertion is assumed. Reverse the unsuccessful holder tilt cautiously while keeping yellow clear, aiming to make its mouth visible before continuing.
Move the holder to a clear area on the right and lower it for a supported regrasp. Its current in-hand orientation is unreliable; keep yellow safely held.
Set the empty holder onto the table and release it for a more stable regrasp. Withdraw the right jaws slightly to reveal its resting orientation; yellow remains held.
Clear the released holder upward and to the right so its resting mouth and body can be seen before regrasping. Keep the yellow pen retained in the left hand.
Reapproach the resting holder from above with open jaws, aiming for its middle rather than its rim. Yellow remains held safely clear.
Align the downward-facing right jaws across the holder's middle and descend to a pregrasp height. Keep the yellow pen stationary and clear.
Lower the right gripping region around the holder's body and close without sliding it. Check retention with a lift next; yellow remains held clear.
The right wrist now appears to see the holder interior. Lift without rotation to verify the new grasp and uprightness before changing its orientation.
The regrasp is retained but the holder's long axis remains horizontal. Rotate its rear-facing mouth upward in a controlled arc while lifting clear and bringing it toward the center.
Complete the holder's upright rotation from the new middle-body grasp and position it near the center at insertion height. Keep yellow clear until the opening is confirmed.
The regrasped holder is upright with its opening visible. Align the yellow pen laterally above the mouth, adding a little clearance and holding the cup fixed.
The yellow pen is leaning toward the left rim. Correct its tilt and center its lower end over the opening before descending; keep the holder stationary.
Lower the yellow pen toward the center of the visible cup opening with only a small forward correction. Stop short of a deep push and inspect entry.
The yellow lower end is visible over the interior. Lower it gently into the empty holder with a small rightward correction, keeping the cup fixed.
Release the yellow pen at its current insertion depth and withdraw upward-left without pushing farther. Check that it settles inside the upright held cup.
Yellow remains in the upright holder. Keep the right grasp fixed and withdraw the left arm toward the white pen, beginning its top-down approach.
Approach above the white pen while continuing the left wrist's downward reorientation. Keep the holder and inserted yellow pen stationary.
Complete the top-down left approach over the white pen, aligning its length between the jaws before the final descent.
Lower the left jaws around the white pen's upper body with a small centering adjustment. Keep the holder and yellow pen undisturbed.
